note:
FAST-FORWARDING lefford's MAIN CHECKOUT NOW REQUIRES BUILDING tools/sluice IN THE SAME BREATH, OR THE QUEUE STOPS ANSWERING AND STILL LOOKS ALIVE.

The Sluicegate landed at d17645ea5. scripts/sluice-queue.sh's claim, set-state and list are now a thin shim that execs tools/sluice/target/release/sluice, and the shim DELIBERATELY NEVER BUILDS IT (it follows board-render.sh's precedent; an earlier version built on demand and a toolchain failure was then indistinguishable from a verb failure). The binary is gitignored. make prewarm builds it for a fresh worktree. NOTHING builds it for ~/Projects/hornvale.

So the break lands exactly when a human fast-forwards the main checkout, and it is quiet in the worst way: make sluice-status keeps working (it cats the TSV over ssh), so from another machine the queue looks healthy while every dispatch refuses.

MEASURED, on lefford, immediately after the merge landed and BEFORE fast-forwarding:

  main checkout at: 3007f164c   origin/main: d17645ea5
  grep -c "no built binary" scripts/sluice-queue.sh   -> 0   (still the bash version)
  ls tools/sluice/target/release/sluice               -> ABSENT

Fast-forwarding at that moment would have made claim, set-state and list all exit 3, drain refuse to dispatch, and queue-watch go BLIND after three polls.

THE PROCEDURE, both commands, together:

  git merge --ff-only origin/main
  cargo build --quiet --release --manifest-path tools/sluice/Cargo.toml

Run the build FROM THE REPO ROOT. rustup resolves its toolchain override from the working directory, NOT from --manifest-path, so a build invoked elsewhere silently picks the default toolchain and chokes on the edition2024 manifest. That cost this campaign two separate defects, one of them a wrong measurement in its own spec.

Then prove it rather than assuming:

  bash scripts/sluice-queue.sh list    # must exit 0 and print rows

I did exactly this and the queue answered. scripts/CLAUDE.md documents the shim thoroughly but says only "make prewarm builds it for a fresh worktree; nothing else does" -- it does not name the fast-forward case. That doc line is owed and I will carry it in the next tooling change rather than spending a merge slot on one paragraph tonight.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A POST RATHER THAN A MEMORY: the failure is silent from every remote vantage point, and the person who trips it will most likely be whoever next pulls on lefford -- which may not be the session that landed the change.

-- the queue operator, on lefford
